newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen edge to new highs on Nikkei losses.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen edge to new highs on Nikkei losses.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures inched towards new contract highs on Friday on the back of losses in Tokyo stocks, which were dragged down by rumours about the financial stability of a Japanese construction company.
But dealers said volumes were very low and interest limited with many local as well as Hong Kong players out for the Chinese New Year holiday.
September Euroyen ended at a new high of 99.38 against its IMM close at 99.36. December finished steady and two ticks off a high of 99.27. Turnover for both months was below 4,200 lots.
"We could see some more buying on Monday," said a trader with a Japanese house, adding that both contracts showed upside potential of about two ticks.
"The Euroyen curve is as flat as it's going to get. It's forecasting unchanged rates through the summer," said a trader with a European house.
Japanese government bond futures for March settled at 126.49 against their previous 126.10.
Dealers said players would focus on the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for January, due at 1330 GMT, and a weekend meeting of finance ministers from the Group of Seven industrialised nations.
The trader with the European house said Japanese funds could take profits on their positions in U.S. treasuries if the payrolls number was far below expectations.
"They need to repatriate funds before the year end. And this would give them good treasury gains and foreign exchange gains," he said, citing the dollar's recent bull run against the yen.
In a Reuters poll, Wall Street analysts said they expected an average increase of 237,000 jobs in January non-farm payrolls against a 262,000 gain the previous month.
"Anything over 300,000 is going to put a negative spin on the market," said the trader.
September Eurodollars ended at 94.18 against its IMM close at 94.17 on 1,800 lots.
